steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 9.06 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.53 in along the bark corner of sawn 2, down to 0.50 in along the point. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 0.00 in along the point; 0.00 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 0.00 in along the bark corner of sawn 2. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Cut 3 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 8.31 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, 0.00 in along the point. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 5.62° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.74 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 71.56 in along the point; 62.35 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 63.80 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 9.15 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 7.70 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 22: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

recipes.name: Run 23
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 8.45 in long. Write 23 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.53 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, down to 0.50 in along the point. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 63.80 in along the point; 73.67 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 78.83 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 7.70 in along the point. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 23: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Shims: bandsaw a few eighths into 1/32 slices for the bark-to-bark seams.
Rip flush: the standing pieces are taller than the frame; rip 1.20 in off the bark so they sit flush with both faces.
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
23 ends: mitre 0.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
23 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece, flipped, lies flat on the frame's 45° slope: sawn face on sawn face, a full-width bearing.
The thin slice in each bark-to-bark seam fills the lens of air and wedges the next full piece tight.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
